    • Searches for “classic toy train set” climbed 240% this year, one of the biggest jumps Google shared.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, each November, Google gives us a peek behind the curtain, synthesising billions of shopping-related searches into their Holiday 100 Gift Guide. The list is built from a full year of Search trends across every category from tech to style. And this year, the toys and games section looks suspiciously like the inside of an elder millennial’s childhood toy chest.

    Here are the trending toys parents will want to know about, plus what the list says about how we’re shopping this year.

    Searches for “classic toy train set” climbed 240% this year, one of the biggest jumps Google shared. Wooden trains survive toddler teeth, being thrown down the stairs and never fail to get passed down more than once. (Expect the figure-eight to claim your living room floor for the next few years.).

    “A ton of play,” Google wrote, and we respect the pun. Searches for stuffed elephant plushies rose 240%, with the Pets Alive Baby Elephant Surprise as the featured pick. Plush is a good pick for a 1-year-old and a 10-year-old alike, and the right one becomes a friend for life.

    According to recent reports, searches for the Fujifilm instax holiday set jumped 190%. For tweens, a camera that spits out a real photo is a nice break from the phone, and the prints end up taped to bedroom walls instead of buried in a camera roll. They’ll fly through the film, so tuck a couple of extra packs in the box.

    Searches for the FAO Schwarz Piano Mat “struck a chord,” rising 180% in 2026. Anyone who watched Tom Hanks stomp out a duet on the giant keyboard in “Major” wanted one of these, and the floor-sized version now fits in a playroom. It’s a sneaky music-and-movement toy for preschoolers. It’s also loud, so choose its permanent residence carefully.

    Searches for “adjustable roller skates” cruised up 180%. Adjustable skates expand across several sizes, so they can outlast a growth spurt or two. Just remember to add a helmet and pads to the cart.

    Some of this may come down to who’s doing the shopping. Millennials make up a big share of today’s parents, and plenty of us spent our childhoods at the roller rink, building wooden train tracks across the living room rug and waiting for Polaroids to develop. (By impatiently wagging them back and forth, of course.) It’s not hard to imagine a few of these searches coming from parents trying to hand down something that felt magic to them. The best part? There’s a good chance they’ll all still be in rotation when next year’s list comes out.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Just one of the Boys raising two girls.

    AJ McLean, the singer, songwriter, and most tattooed member of The Backstreet Boys just moved his family to Latest York City. “All three of the ladies in my life love New York,” he says — and he’s all about it. “Celebrating Christmas in New York this year is going to be fantastic.”.

    But before he can take the family to the Rockettes, McLean has an album to launch (Sex, Love, and Music, out Nov. 27) and a solo tour to rock (The Better Man Tour). He is also busy as the spokesman for Delsym 12-Hour Cough Relief, which he states saved a performance during The Backstreet Boys residency at The Sphere last year. McLean took a break from his tour to take Fatherly’s Cool Dad questionnaire — and talk about staying healthy, sober, and putting family first.

    I think I am a cool dad. I think I'm a cool dad because I really kind of let my kids form their own opinions and have a voice, and we work as a team. I want my girls to always have a voice. That's super important to me. Sometimes, they have too much of a voice, but it's OK. That's when dad has to step in and reel it back a little bit. I want my girls to just always look up to their dad, and I try to set the best example that I can.

    AJ McLean on his solo “The Better Man” Tour.

    What's the best film to watch with kids?

    So I'm an ’80s kid and I am so happy that I turned my girls onto Labyrinth, which they absolutely love; The Goonies, which they absolutely love; and Gremlins. They are obsessed, especially with Labyrinth. When I mentioned it to them, they were a little hesitant, and then once we watched it, I went back to work and caught wind from the wife that they've watched it repeatedly days after, and I'm like, "Yes, I did it.".

    What's one thing you wish your kids had today that you had growing up, especially as a kid from the ’80s?

    I wish they had cassette tape players. I did get a cassette tape player gift box from my boys over at Aerosmith, and it came with a cassette tape of their upcoming album — it was a promotional thing. And I indicated it to my daughters, and they did not know what they were looking at. They put it in backwards. I'm like, "No, no, no, no, no, no." And then they were like, "What is the red button?" I noted, "No, that's for recording." And they were astounded when I pressed play and this little speaker was playing and I'm like, "When your dad was growing up, that was it. That's all we had. There was no Bose surround sound, there was none of that.".

    Recent findings suggest that and then my youngest — last year as a birthday present from one of her friends — got a Discman. And she of course put the CD in upside down, I had to show her the right way. That was painful. But she really loves her freaking Discman. She loves it. And I love that they're starting to come back where you actually have to buy the CD. I keep telling my girls, "There's pictures in there; there's thank yous; there's a whole thing. It's not just listening to the music; it's a whole package deal, where you don't get that if you're listening to iTunes. You see one picture and listen to the music, that's it. Albums were a thing." So I'm starting to get them into that now, which I really love.

    What's music have you successfully introduced your kids to?

    My oldest daughter's first album was The Beatles’ White Album. She learned every word between the ages of 2 and 3. And she was a sponge. My wife is the biggest Beatles fan out of anyone I've ever met in my life. She is diehard. So that was her first album. She's like, "This is what my kids are listening to, Beatles." I'm like, "OK.".

    AJ McLean and his family, pictured here in 2022, recently moved to Fresh York City.

    And what music have your kids introduced you to?

    Recent findings suggest that recently, I took the family to the premiere of Michael, and my daughters knew who Michael Jackson was, but after the film, the obsession was over the top. They know songs I've never heard, deep cuts. People forget about Michael's Jackson’s Xscape album and they're saying, "Dad, play such and such a song." And I'm like, "That's not a song." They're like, "Yes, it is." They know more music, I think, now than I've ever known in my entire life. We have a very musical family, very musical family.

    What does fatherhood mean to you in the current world?

    Fatherhood, to me, means protection. It means compassion, understanding. It means listening with my ears and not my mouth, and being nonjudgmental, which I'm a very nonjudgmental person anyways, but just by nature, that's how I was raised. And trying to really broaden my daughters’ spectrum of the world, and to love everyone, and to accept everyone, and to be colorblind, to be genderblind, to be just very open and loving. And they are. They are two of the coolest kids I think any father could ever ask for. They are super smart. They are loving kids. They are people, people like me.

    They're not shy by any means. They will talk to everybody and talk their ear off, and I have no idea where they get that from. But yeah, I try to just really set an example, especially as a father and as a man, I want my daughters to look at me and then be able to say when the time comes that they want to date boys, this is what a boy should be. This is what a man should be, like, respectful. And I grew up single-parent household, so I grew up to very much so respect women to the utmost, and put them up on a pedestal, which it's kind of a give and take, but to really know that none of us would be here without a woman, let's just say that.

    What piece of clothing or gear are you really passionate about right now? What do you can't get enough of?

    Sources indicate that I mean, I'm a sneakerhead. I have a problem. And I've gotten my girls into it now, which my wife is so thrilled about.

    According to recent reports, well, it's easier for me because I'm done. My foot's where it's at, it ain't going up, it ain't going down, but my daughters are still growing. So when I go get a pair of Jordans that are like $200 and then my kids want to match daddy's shoes, it's a little like they're going to be in them for six months and then they're going to be out of them. But then we donate them anyway, so we're not just throwing them out; we're donating them.

    What are you wearing right now then? What's on your feet?

    In a recent development, right now, I've got my travel shoes, which are my Adidas Ultraboost, but my everyday shoes are [Jordan] 1s or 3s. That is my go-to. My collection has gotten pretty large. And my daughters now, they're nowhere near as many as me, but they're starting to catch up.

    What does Rochelle love about you?

    I think she loves my heart, my generosity, my kindness, my ability to be very comforting and loving. I'm a very affectionate person. I try to be a very loyal person. I try to be a very honest person. I have my faults; nobody's perfect. I tell people I'm perfectly imperfect. And I think she just loves me for me. I think even more so now, being sober for over five years and living my true authentic self, our relationship now I think is the best it's ever been, being in each other's lives for 15 years.

    Recent findings suggest that we went through some tough stuff. We separated, we were living separately, and we both now can look back and reflect on what needed to happen. There are no mistakes. I believe everything happens exactly how it's meant to be. We needed that time apart to grow individually and to grow as a unit. And now, we're living together as a family for the first time in almost four years. We're renting a place in New York so my girls can go to an incredible dance school, and all three of the ladies in my life love New York, and they would've moved there years ago.

    They're having the time of their life. And I told them, because we actually moved the tail end of summer, and none of my girls have ever experienced humidity or the heat that is the East Coast.

    And I would FaceTime them and be like, "Oh, dear God, what's with your hair?" But now they understand.

    Now they know that everyone leaves the city in the summer, so you'll do that next year.

    Exactly. But celebrating Christmas in Latest York this year is going to be fantastic.

    Alexandra Zatarain helped build Eight Sleep into a tech unicorn, and she’s expecting her first child in January. Going through pregnancy while running a global company has reshaped how she sees her own body, her industry and the product she’s building. On this episode of The Motherly Podcast, the co-founder of the sleep-technology company talks about the research that showed Eight Sleep’s technology was improving men’s sleep more than women’s and what the company did about it, why sleep is the most crucial thing women can protect, and the career advice she wishes more women heard before becoming mothers.

    Meet the expert: Alexandra Zatarain is the co-founder and VP of brand and marketing at Eight Sleep, the sleep-technology firm behind the Pod. The Pod is an intelligent mattress cover that cools or heats each side to your ideal temperature automatically, maximizing deep sleep and minimizing wake-ups. A marketer and brand builder, she grew Eight Sleep from launch into a tech unicorn and helped create what the company calls the sleep fitness movement. Eight Sleep now sells in 37 countries. She’s expecting her first child in January with her husband, Matteo, the company’s co-founder and CEO.

    According to recent reports, alexandra Zatarain: So many things. I just turned 37, and I’ve seen so many friends go through pregnancy before me. After my first trimester, I felt so bad, thinking, what a terrible friend I was. When you haven’t experienced it, you have such little empathy for what a woman’s body is going through, especially when life keeps demanding so much of you and it doesn’t stop. I really didn’t understand that you could feel so different in your body for so long. It’s built so much more admiration for women and what we go through, and it’s let me embrace a feminine side of myself that in tech you usually don’t get to bring out.

    Sources indicate that alexandra Zatarain: It’s made me realize that the only way the world out there is going to change for our benefit as women and mothers is if more of us are the ones making the decisions. I just don’t see any way around it. We have a lot of parents at Eight Sleep, every executive on our team is a parent, but as a woman the experience is completely different. Unless we can share that first-hand knowledge, it’s going to be hard to make progress as fast as we need to. It’s unfortunate that it takes the first-person experience to become that advocate, because everyone should appreciate what mothers go through, given that we all come from a mother.

    Recent findings suggest that alexandra Zatarain: A couple of years ago, our clinical team, which is more than 90% women, was analyzing data from our user base and noticed our technology had been improving men’s sleep more than women’s. They asked, what are we missing in how we design this? It turned out the algorithms that manage temperature while you sleep had been fed more data representing men than women. That’s a classic problem in science, where women are underrepresented because our bodies are more complex. You have to account for where someone is in their hormonal journey, pregnancy, postpartum, perimenopause. So we invested a couple million dollars into research and developed features from it. That changed how we think about ourselves, less about helping everyone in a broad way and more about solving specific problems women have had for ages.

    Industry observers note that alexandra Zatarain: Sleep is the most notable pillar of health. You would die sooner from sleep deprivation than from food deprivation, which tells you how fundamental it is. For women it matters even more because our hormones rule our lives, and sleep is the one tool we have to regulate them. If you sleep well, your chances of better hormonal balance go up significantly. It’s the best medicine we have, more than working out, more than any meal. The challenge is that those same hormones are often playing against us, making it harder to sleep well in different seasons of life, so keeping our routines as stable as possible helps counter what our bodies are going through.

    Alexandra Zatarain: The mindset piece is really key. There’s so much going on, the anxiety, the intrusive thoughts, so not being too hard on yourself is the first step. Understanding that the season will pass should put you a little more at ease, because it’s not going to be your life forever. The other piece is setting yourself up with the right systems, and the most important one is available to everyone for free, which is routine. It helps your body a lot. When you do need to sleep, it’ll be easier for your body to fall asleep because it’s used to the schedule.

    It has been revealed that alexandra Zatarain: I’m very rigid about my sleep schedule. I travel a lot, so sleep is number one for me. I make space for eight to nine hours every night, and I’m pretty good at hitting it. I go to bed by 9:30 or 10 every single night no matter where I am in the world, and I don’t really use an alarm unless I have to wake up before 6, because my body just wakes up on its own. That schedule is the thing that’s changed my life the most. Second to that is the environment, the temperature in my room and my bed, the lights going dark, no noise.

    Alexandra Zatarain: I think of myself as an athlete, and we’re all sort of athletes in a way. My sport is making decisions about how to build this business, and that means I have to train, stay healthy and think long term. It’s not a sprint. We’ve been doing this for 12 years, so the question is how do I not burn out and stay here 20 or 30 years more. I’m also lucky I built this with my husband, so there’s no real line between business and personal life for us. It’s all mixed in, but it’s so purpose-driven that achieving that purpose every day is what feeds the energy.

    Alexandra Zatarain: I’m very open with them about how intentional I was. I did my embryo freezing in my early 30s because of where I was in life. And I tell them that if they want a career after they have a family, the best time to build equity in that career is to push as hard as you can before. Know what you want, because time isn’t always on our side as women. Move up the ranks, so that by the time you have kids you have more flexibility and maybe a higher income. It is possible, but it takes planning, it will require compromises, and very importantly it will require the right partner.

    Alexandra Zatarain: It starts with the people around you understanding what you truly need. Sometimes it’s as simple as the encouragement of, yes, go take a nap, yes, your body’s going through a lot. It gets harder once the baby’s home and the mom is maybe exclusively breastfeeding, because it really all falls on you. So have a plan in place ahead of time for how the load is going to be shared. Our partners are much more involved than previous generations, so have those conversations early. It doesn’t end with the birth plan. That’s where everything starts.

    Alexandra Zatarain: The first trimester was difficult, a lot of nausea, and it was very hard to function at the level I’m used to. I almost never get sick, so feeling sick every day was a huge shift. It put me in the trajectory to build the team that would make it possible for me to become a mother, to figure out what to delegate and who to elevate, and I’ve built a stronger team as a result. But the biggest thing is that it’s taught me to let go. I can’t control how I feel every day. As a Type A person I always want to be in control, and this has been like therapy, learning that I’m not in control of my body. I’m building a human, and it’s fine if for this season things just work differently.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I don’t care if I’m reliant on it and you can’t make me.

    Sleep deprivation is a form of torture. At some point in every adult’s life, you find out why the hard way. Every parent goes through intense sleep deprivation when they bring home their first baby, and every subsequent newborn after that. But for some of us, sleep never came easy. By the time the babies came on the scene, we were well acquainted with the wee hours of the morning, what it felt like to be up all night, every night.

    According to recent reports, as a kid, I remember lying in bed for long stretches of time before I could fall asleep. My thoughts would race about everything and nothing. I had a dream catcher above my bed to ward off nightmares, worry dolls under my pillow to whisper my anxieties to so they could “hold them for me” until the morning, and my bedroom TV volume on low while a plucky Disney Channel show played. At sleepovers I was always the last to fall asleep, if I managed to stay overnight at all.

    I didn’t get a formal anxiety diagnosis until I went off to college many years later, but learning more about my brain finally gave me an understanding of why sleep was so elusive. With a nervous system stuck in fight-or-flight mode, of course I’d wake at the slightest sound and have a nearly impossible time winding down enough to knock out at the end of the day.

    Finally, in 2019, I expressed my frustrations to my fresh psychiatrist. I was awake for hours every night waiting for sleep to come, while my husband was already in REM before he ever got fully horizontal on the mattress. I tried guided meditations (why do all the beach ones feature squawking seagulls?) and binaural beats and exercising with the goal of exhausting myself during the day, but my insomnia had reached a frustrating new intensity. It was making my anxiety and depression so much worse; I looked and felt utterly bedraggled. So, he prescribed me trazodone.

    Sources indicate that while trazodone isn’t a true sedative — it’s actually an antidepressant — it’s often used off-label to treat insomnia because it gives you a similar relaxing, drowsy feeling. My doctor told me that it’s not a controlled substance and carries a very low risk of addiction, but that mentally, I might start to feel like I need it in order to sleep. If I didn’t like feeling dependent on it, we could make some changes.

    “Are they going to stop making it any time soon?” I asked.

    “Is it bad to take long-term for any other reason?”.

    Sources indicate that “Then I’m perfectly fine with being mentally addicted,” I stated. And I’ve taken it every single night since then.

    Research has shown again and again that regularly sleeping well is a key quality-of-life indicator. Lack of sleep negatively impacts every system of the body, weakening the immune system, worsening mental health, and increasing risk of countless conditions, from high cholesterol to Alzheimer’s. Women are twice as likely to have insomnia as men, which has been attributed to our natural hormonal fluctuations throughout the month and the fact that we tend to carry the lion’s share of the mental load in the family, on top of being more prone to mood disorders.

    Yet even though we know all of this, taking anything to help you fall asleep is still... kind of frowned upon. Researchers in the UK conducted focus groups interviewing people who take prescription sleep medications and OTC supplements, like melatonin, and found that they had a lot of internalized stigma around the subject — even when talking about it in a room full of people who also take something to help them sleep.

    It has been revealed that they found that participants were very deliberate in how they explained their need for their meds. They’re deserving (explaining that their condition, like chronic pain or anxiety, makes sleep impossible without medication). They’re compliant, only ever taking their meds exactly as prescribed (or, in the case of supplements, as directed on the label). They’re responsible, always watching themselves for signs of addiction or misuse. They expressed extreme guilt over taking more of their medications than they should, or trying alternative medications meant to make them sleepy when their usual prescription wasn’t enough.

    We recently asked Scary Mommy’s Instagram followers the question, “Do you take anything to fall asleep at night?” Some of that same stigma showed up in their responses too.

    Multiple readers remarked they take Gravol when they can’t sleep, calling it a “horrid habit” or something they only do “when things get really bad.” Another said, “I can’t sleep without a quarter of an Ambien. It’s terrible!” “Haven’t had an unmedicated sleep in 7+ years 🫠,” said one response. The melting face is doing a lot of heavy lifting there.

    Of course there were plenty of Scary Mommies who felt no shame (that’s sort of our shtick around here). In response to the question “Do you take anything to fall asleep?” one user simply replied, “WINE.” Plenty of other respondents also take trazodone, or Unisom, or some other sleep aid. Weed, whether in vape or gummy form, is also an extremely popular option. See also: a large number of replies indicating they take magnesium and progesterone at night thanks to perimenopause, and that HRT was finally the thing to help them sleep through the night.

    But one response really captures my feelings about the whole subject:.

    “Oh lord I’m so medicated. But it’s working.”.

    Even on the days I feel like I shouldn’t have to take something to help me sleep, that perhaps I could sleepmaxx or wellness hack my way out of having to take a pill every night, I remind myself that not getting enough sleep is literally deadly.

    In a recent development, when you’re someone who struggles with sleep night after night, you know how quickly your mental and physical health can plummet. Insomnia decimates my quality of life. Sleep deprivation locks my personality and my joy away behind a concrete wall where I can’t access them anymore. It impacts my longevity and my relationships. While I’m not saying every reader who responded has a healthy way of getting to sleep at night, or that we shouldn’t be critical of our relationships with substances, I think we could all use a little validation that not getting enough sleep is, in fact, torturous.

    In a recent development, more moms need to hear that they deserve to sleep well. They should know that their doctors want to hear from them if they feel abnormally tired during the day. And I want more women to internalize the idea that this world is hard enough to live in as it is. You should at least be able to meet it each day not feeling like a shell of yourself.

    And that’s why you can pry my trazodone out of my cold, dead hands.

    • Here are some of our favorite travel-forward finds.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    You can never go wrong with travel gifts, TBH.

    It has been revealed that some clichés are clichés for a reason. Being a mom is really hard. But it’s so, so rewarding. Also, travel is the best teacher. For many moms, those three clichés are often true in tandem. Sometimes, the lessons we learn during travel make the invisible load of motherhood a little lighter to bear. Sometimes, the lesson is simply that we have to make time for ourselves to be the best moms we can be. And sometimes, seeing the world through our kids’ eyes is enough to remind us that even when the road is rough, the reward is usually worth it.

    So, when it comes to gifts you can give the moms in your life, it’s hard to beat travel gifts... especially when travel already seems to be their favorite form of therapy. While splurging on things as pricey as plane tickets or an all-inclusive resort stay is (understandably) out of reach for many of us, there are tons of items any travel-loving mom would be overjoyed to get. We should know! The Scary Mommy editors are all busy moms who enjoy squeezing getaways and adventures into whatever little pockets of spare time we can find.

    Here are some of our favorite travel-forward finds.

    According to recent reports, I have the full-size Naturepedic pillow, and I yearn to own the travel-sized one too. I have chronic neck pain and headaches, so I need a soft yet supportive pillow and one that is comfortable when sleeping on my back or my side. I’ve purchased and used so many pillows in my day, and this is finally THE ONE. I love that you can customize how much stuffing you keep inside, and I like to form mine with a little divot for my head to maximize my neck support. The full-size is heavy, though, so I really want to find a travel-sized one under the tree this year to use instead of the down (deeply unsupportive) hotel pillows that leave me hurting. — Katie McPherson, Associate Editor, Lifestyle & Entertainment.

    Industry observers note that this is the diaper bag I wish I’d had for every family trip with little ones! It fits a pump, bottles, diapers, a laptop... really, you’d be surprised how much stuff you can stuff in it. I especially love that there’s a quick-grab pocket on the front sized perfectly for wipes. Even though my kids are teens, I carry this as a carry-on backpack because it’s so pretty and functional, and it slips right over your suitcase handle so you have one less thing to juggle at the gate. Thanks to the easy-clean neoprene and chic design, it doesn’t scream “diaper bag.” — Julie Sprankles, Deputy Editor, Lifestyle & Entertainment.

    The Cincha Go-Tote has become my most-reached-for travel bag because it solves the one problem every traveler has: The carry-on that tips over every time you let go of it. The Cincha Go-Tote has a built-in luggage sleeve that slides right over your suitcase handle so everything stays put, and your hands stay free; plus it is water-resistant, has leather accents that make it look way more elevated than a travel bag has any right to look, and fits everything you need for a flight without becoming a black hole. This is for the traveler on your holiday list who has everything but still somehow does not have this. — Katie Garrity, Senior Editor, News & Social.

    I have bought my fair share of travel pillows over the years, and a lot of them just... don't get the job done. I love this one because it stuffs into a small sack and it really does help you nod off on the plane without choking or smothering you. When I travel with this, people always ask me where it's from. — Sarah Aswell, Deputy Editor, News & Social.

    Sources indicate that I think my new favorite obsession is traveling with a trunk! For those trips when you need the extra space, this beauty lets you travel in style. It has such a sophisticated vintage-inspired look... it feels like it should be loaded onto the Orient Express. That old-world glamour even extends to a sleek double-latch closure (instead of a zipper) with TSA-approved locks. She’s not just pretty, though; she’s durable too, thanks to a tough polycarbonate shell, reinforced corners, and replaceable wheels. And once you get used to traveling trunk-style with its super-convenient deep side, it’ll be hard to go back! — Julie Sprankles.

    It has been revealed that packing for a trip with kids usually means digging through a black hole for one sock, and these clear, color-coded organizers fix that. The set of four comes in big, medium, and mini sizes with windows so you can see exactly what’s inside, and my favorite part is that each one gets its own job, like clothes, snacks, or tech and first aid. They’re the unglamorous travel upgrade that makes packing and unpacking take minutes instead of hours, and I’m never traveling without them again!— Katie Garrity.

    According to recent reports, I don't know how many times I've had a fully charged battery back with me while traveling, but I can't find the right cord to attach it to my phone. This magnetic charger is small, mighty, and charges cordlessly! It has become my number one charging brick, and that claims a lot coming from me. This is one of those products where you buy one and then almost immediately buy another one, just to have a spare. I also love getting these as gifts for people! — Sarah Aswell.

    My non-negotiable for travel days is comfort, but I don’t want to look like I rolled right out of bed and onto the plane, either. These Cozy Earth joggers are just the ticket. They’re ridiculously soft, with a slim-but-relaxed fit and an adjustable drawstring that’s perfect for long flights. And the burgundy color is seriously stunning, so I look put-together even though I feel like I’m in my comfiest PJs. — Julie Sprankles.

    Ask anyone who knows me, and they'll tell you my happy place is sitting out in the sun — wherever that may be. As someone who has long loved Gray Malin's art (but not someone who has been able to splurge on it as often as I'd like), these travel pouches make a great happy medium. I love how packable and useful these travel pouches are, but what I love most about them is how "in the mood" they'll get you to travel. As you pack up your stuff, you can practically taste vacation. What's not to love? — Kate Auletta, Editor in Chief.

    For the traveler on your list who is still hauling around a beat-up suitcase, this is the upgrade that will make them feel like a seasoned jet-setter, with a slim aluminum frame and polycarbonate shell that look as sleek as they are tough. The 77-liter interior has a built-in compression panel for squeezing in just a little more and about 1.5 inches of extra depth, which is exactly what you need for a 7- to 10-day trip. It also has 360° spinner wheels and two TSA-approved locks, so it’s the gift that makes every airport trip a little less stressful! — Katie Garrity.

    Sources indicate that like many people entering their 40s after a lifetime of wear and tear, I deal with a lot of foot issues, especially when I'm walking 20,000 steps a day while traveling. I love these shoe inserts that have gotten me through the most epic travel days, including 12-mile days at Disney World and a 15-mile day hike in Glacier National Park. — Sarah Aswell.

    While experts generally agree that airlines don’t reuse blankets, it’s still comforting just to carry your own on board. As someone who is always cold, I can’t tell you how much I appreciate being able to toss this into my carry-on. It comes with a super-soft throw, a matching eye mask, and the coordinating bag to stash them both in. — Julie Sprankles.

    This is the carry-on to match all carry-ons! This backpack opens super wide at the top so you can find anything you need, plus it has a large front zippered pocket for chargers, snacks, or notes from admirers. It fits so much stuff and yet still somehow slides perfectly under an airplane seat like some kind of backpack sorcery. — Katie Garrity.

    It’s just designed to fit so much more, even though it takes up the same amount of space as other bags. Used with the packing cubes from the same firm, I can easily fit a week’s worth of stuff into a bag and not have to check anything. — Sarah Aswell.

    Recent findings suggest that marshall is such an iconic brand that I feel a little cooler every time I slip these headphones on. There are lots of reasons they’re great for tossing in your carry-on. The adaptive noise cancellation automatically blocks out plane noises, but one push of a button switches to transparency mode so I can hear flight announcements. The battery lasts up to 50-plus hours with ANC on. And, one of my favorite features, they’re made to fold up small so you can stash them in your bag without a hassle. — Julie Sprankles.

    This tote organizer turns any bottomless pit of a bag into an orderly dream. With pockets and pouches for all of your on-the-go essentials, the ToteSavvy makes traveling a breeze. — Katie Garrity.

    S'well makes my favorite lunch salad bowl container; it never leaks and is super high-quality. So when I saw that the same company came out with a travel bottle set, I knew that I wanted it! All of their products are so well-designed and thoughtful; these bottles are made of lightweight material, and they haven't leaked yet. They also come in a super cute lightweight pouch. — Sarah Aswell.

    My husband travels for work, so he flies multiple times per week. He’s been using the Airback MAX for about a year now, and it has held up remarkably well to his strenuous schedule! But what he really loves is that it lets him skip checking a bag because it has a built-in vacuum system that sucks air out of your clothes. That means you can fit 25+ items in this one carry-on-sized bag. It also converts from a rolling trolley to a backpack in seconds, has dual TSA-approved locks, USB ports, and an expandable compression bag that doubles as a laundry bag. — Julie Sprankles.

    The scariest part of any flight is wondering how long the entertainment is going to last, and this kit is built to keep toddlers 18 months and up busy from takeoff to landing without a single screen. It comes with a first-flight storybook that helps set expectations before you board, which is a small thing that makes a major difference when a little one has never been on a plane. It’s compact, screen-free, and designed by Lovevery’s play experts, so it’s one more thing I don’t have to worry about in the carry-on. — Katie Garrity.

    Sources indicate that for a bag that barely weighs a pound when unpacked and tucks away neatly into a small zippered square, you’ll be shocked by how much The Foldie actually holds: When fully expanded, it has a 40-liter packing volume. The expandable bottom adds just the right amount of extra space when needed. We love that it’s a great size to use as your carry-on or to tuck into your suitcase for bringing home souvenirs. I’ve been using this bag heavily for almost two years now, and it’s still one of my absolute favorites. Not only does it still look great, but I get asked about it all the time! — Julie Sprankles.

    I fully admit I got one of these after seeing a social media video of a before-and-after. This thing really does depuff your face... and if you're like me, my face can get pretty puffy while traveling. Carrying this with me and having it after I get off the plane or after a long car ride just makes me feel better. And even besides the de-puffing benefits, it feels really good, too. — Sarah Aswell.

    Industry observers note that I love that the Woda is the brainchild of two moms living in Charleston, South Carolina, who needed something hands-free that could be hosed down after days on the coast with their kids. For moms who love to pack up the car and head to the nearest beach as much as possible, you can’t get a better gift than this super-durable yet lightweight waterproof backpack. Made from a non-toxic EVA foam, it’s mold- and mildew-resistant, meaning she won’t have to worry about it getting funky after a day on the water. And it’s seriously roomy with a carrying capacity of up to 30 pounds! — Julie Sprankles.

    According to recent reports, any traveler knows long flights cause blood flow in the legs to slow down since you’re seated for extended periods. That, in turn, can increase the risk of health complications like deep vein thrombosis. Compression socks are a simple way to help blood vessels work more efficiently on long flights, reducing the risk of swelling and blood clots. Trust us when we say that Dr. Motion compression socks are out here compressioning! And they come in so many cute patterns, which is so girly to say... but we don’t care. — Katie Garrity.

    According to recent reports, what did I do before packing cubes? I love these by JanSport because they are larger than most and fit perfectly in my suitcase side by side. The smaller "cube" is great for carrying an extra pair of undies and a spare shirt in my carry-on. They also have a see-through mesh front and a carrying handle, which make a huge difference. And never forget that JanSport items all come with an incredibly wonderful lifetime warranty. — Sarah Aswell.

    In a recent development, I’m a carry-on girlie whenever I can be, but some trips just require more space. And if I’m going to be checking a bag, I want it to fit everything without being too cumbersome. This Monos Medium Check-in is the perfect size because it’s roomy without being obnoxiously big. Plus, the limited-edition Mulberry color is a deep, glossy purple that is beyond dreamy! Add in the fact that it’s durable, has a TSA-accepted lock, and super-glidable wheels, and I genuinely get excited at the mere thought of packing for my next trip. — Julie Sprankles.

    Sources indicate that it’s a toss-up when it comes to what’s more vexing: using generic hotel bar soap to wash your face or having to buy new face wash when you get where you’re going because you can’t carry on your fave. That’s why I’m a significant fan of Olay Cleansing Melts. These portable cleansing squares are TSA-friendly since they’re water-activated, so you can toss ‘em in your purse or carry-on. — Kate Auletta.

    Industry observers note that raise your hand if you’ve ever frantically patted down every pocket in an airport security line, convinced you lost your passport (me, it’s definitely me). This Spotminders Passport Holder Air works with Apple’s Find My app, meaning I can see exactly where my passport is in about two seconds. It’s ultra-slim but still has room for my license and a few other cards, plus a dedicated flap for boarding passes. Right now there’s a buy-two-get-one-free deal, which makes it a smart pick if you’re looking to upgrade the whole family before a massive trip. — Julie Sprankles.

    Sources indicate that for anyone who’s ever stood at the airport counter pulling a sweater out of an overstuffed suitcase, the BÉIS Large Check-In Roller is a game changer, thanks to its built-in weight indicator that tells you when you’re hitting 50 pounds before you ever leave the house. It has a durable hard-shell exterior, 360° wheels, a TSA lock, a hidden AirTag pocket, and 2 inches of expansion for the souvenirs you absolutely will bring home, and the glossy mint color means you’ll spot it on the carousel from across the room.     Sources indicate that for trips when I don’t have room for over-ear headphones, these Nothing Ear (3a) earbuds pack a ton of travel-ready power into a punchy, pocket-sized case. They have active noise cancellation and hi-res sound, plus the battery life is up to 41 hours so I don’t have to hunt for an outlet at the gate. They’re also great for using while on calls. I got the yellow colorway, and it just makes me happy every time I pull them out. — Julie Sprankles.

    Abdulrahman El Bahnasawy, 28, of Ontario, Canada, was sentenced today to 50 years in prison for offenses related to a 2020 attack on correctional officers at U.S. Penitentiary Allenwood. This sentence will run consecutive to the 40-year sentence he is presently serving for his role in plotting a mass-casualty terrorist attack in New York City on behalf of ISIS.

    Industry observers note that “Bahnasawy, who is already serving a 40-year sentence in federal prison for plotting mass casualty attacks in Upcoming York City on behalf of ISIS, savagely attacked corrections officers once again on behalf of ISIS,” noted Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “Today’s sentence will further ensure that Bahnasawy remains in prison, where he can do much less harm, for a very long time.”.

    In a recent development, “We will prosecute those who aid, attempt to aid, or commit violence on behalf of the pernicious ISIS ideology wherever they may be found,” stated U.S. Attorney Brian D. Miller for the Middle District of Pennsylvania. “Today’s sentence reflects our unwavering commitment to fight those who perpetrate violence in the name of ISIS even behind prison walls.”.

    According to recent reports, “Although he was behind bars, this convicted terrorist committed a horrific attack on two corrections officers in the name of ISIS, which they fortunately survived,” said Assistant Director Jarod Brown of the FBI’s Counterterrorism Division. “Today’s sentencing reveals that violent attacks by those who support the evil ideology of ISIS or other foreign terrorist organizations cannot be tolerated by our society. Fighting terrorism is a central part of the FBI’s mission to protect the American people, and the FBI is committed to working with our law enforcement partners to hold these vicious criminals accountable.”.

    Bahnasawy was an inmate at USP Allenwood who, on Dec. 7, 2020, attacked two corrections officers using a weapon made from part of a steel desk in his cell. Bahnasawy stabbed one officer in the head and face, and, when a second responded to assist, Bahnasawy stabbed her in the hand.

    Industry observers note that the first officer eventually lost his right eye as a result of the attack. When Bahnasawy was restrained, a note was found in his sock that read, “This is a terrorist attack for the Islamic State.” A pledge of allegiance to the Islamic State of Iraq and al-Sham (ISIS) was also found taped to the inside of a locker door in Bahnasawy’s prison cell. Bahnasawy pleaded guilty in November 2025 to multiple counts of assault, assault with intent to commit murder, and possession of contraband inside a prison as well as providing material support to ISIS, a designated foreign terrorist organization.

    Recent findings suggest that at the time of the attacks at USP Allenwood, Bahnasawy was serving a 40-year sentence for his role in plotting a mass-casualty terrorist attack in Newly introduced York City on behalf of ISIS. Bahnasawy, a then-20-year-old Canadian citizen and resident, plotted with Talha Haroon and Russell Salic to conduct bombings and shootings in heavily populated areas of New York City during the Islamic holy month of Ramadhan in 2016, all in the name of ISIS.

    An undercover FBI agent (UC) infiltrated the co-conspirators’ terrorist plot, posing as an ISIS supporter prepared to join in the attacks. The FBI arrested Bahnasawy in May 2016 after he traveled from Canada to the Latest York City area in preparation for the attacks, and he has been in custody since that time.

    This case was investigated by the FBI’s Philadelphia Field Office.

    According to recent reports, assistant U.S. Attorney Geoffrey MacArthur for the Middle District of Pennsylvania and Deputy Chief Larry Schneider of the National Security Division’s Counterterrorism Section prosecuted the case.

    #8991. Tech Report: Your kid needs you to have hobbies outside of motherhood. Here’s why

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (912 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mother ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Your kid needs you to have hobbies outside of motherhood. Here’s why

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (912 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mother

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • That’s how long it had been since I last stood atop a swim block, preparing to dive in for a timed race in an official meet.
    • Recent findings suggest that A whistle blew.
    • Recent findings suggest that when I got out of the pool, I walked over to my kids.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Twenty-four years. That’s how long it had been since I last stood atop a swim block, preparing to dive in for a timed race in an official meet.

    Recent findings suggest that A whistle blew. The crowd hushed to silence. A monotone call came over the loudspeaker, “Swimmers, take your mark,” followed by a loud electronic beep that signaled the start of the race. I felt the cold rush of water overtake my body upon diving in. The neurons in my brain feverishly told my muscles to complete the strokes I’d learned decades before. In seconds, it was done. I finished the race.

    Recent findings suggest that when I got out of the pool, I walked over to my kids. My son, a competitive swimmer himself, looked at me and earnestly remarked, “Wow, Mom. I’m proud of you.”.

    Sources indicate that like most moms, I have a packed schedule. I work, parent, volunteer at school, shepherd my two kids to practices and social gatherings, throw meals together, walk the dog, and occasionally find a moment to breathe. But over the past couple of years, I watched my growing kids, now ages 12 and 9, discover and engage in passions that light them up. It left me wondering, why not me, too?

    “A recurring theme in my practice is women feeling they’ve lost their individual identities somewhere between work, parenting, and meeting everyone else’s needs,” says Carly Snyder, a New York City–based reproductive and perinatal psychiatrist. “Part of my work involves helping women recognize that their own interests and needs are legitimate.”.

    Industry observers note that research highlights a multitude of benefits earned by pursuing hobbies. Hobbyists often have wider social networks, improved mental health markers, and enhanced positive emotions.

    Hobbies offer a particularly crucial lifeline for mothers, who often report losing themselves to the demanding needs of family life. That rings true for Kaitlyn Edington, an art educator and mom of two who recalls struggling after returning to work as a teacher following the birth of her first child. “I was so depleted,” Edington indicates. She spent her workdays teaching with short breaks to pump, often bringing her computer into her pumping room so she could catch up on work, then went home to full nights of infant care.

    According to recent reports, one day while scrolling on Instagram, Edington saw an artist posting images of her sketchbook paintings. “She changed my life,” Edington states. “Her sketchbook paintings were so loose and free, and she was encouraging people to draw everyday. I remember thinking, ‘If I have to pump two to three times a day, which I absolutely hate, why not pair it with something that I love?’” From then on, Edington sketched when she pumped, and ultimately developed a habit of daily sketching that she continues 10 years later.

    No longer in the pumping phase of life, Edington ensures she gets time to sketch by waking up before her kids. “I hold the habit of waking up before my kids as sacred,” she indicates. “I need that time, when nobody needs me. It’s my emotional rest.”.

    In a recent development, science backs Edington’s belief that her hobby stabilizes her mental health. “Reengaging in meaningful, enjoyable activities can be therapeutically valuable,” Snyder says. “Behavioral activation, an evidence-based treatment for depression, specifically emphasizes reconnecting with activities that provide pleasure, purpose, or a sense of accomplishment.”.

    Snyder has three children, ages 19, 16, and 11, and throughout their lives she has maintained her dedication to skiing, cycling, yoga and running, completing a total of 19 marathons. She knows her kids benefit from her hobbies. Each time Snyder trains for an upcoming marathon, “[My kids] witness my commitment, discipline, setbacks, and perseverance,” she says. “Watching a parent pursue a hobby provides opportunities to observe persistence, emotional regulation, problem-solving, and enjoyment.”.

    It has been revealed that but those benefits are secondary to the impacts hobbies have on the women pursuing them. “I think we’ve become so accustomed to framing everything mothers do in terms of how it benefits their children,” Snyder says. “Women are entitled to happiness and fulfillment for their own sake.”.

    It’s simply an added bonus that when mom is happy for mom’s sake, the benefits for her kids naturally follow, according to multiple studies linking a mother’s well-being with her child’s. Plus, kids also learn that all stages of adulthood, including those under the umbrella of parenting, can include personal fulfillment, curiosity, and growth.

    Recent findings suggest that the best way to start a hobby is to let yourself reconnect with something you already love. I remembered how much joy I got out of competing in swim meets in high school, and I was eager to recreate that glee. Ask yourself, “What did I love when I was a kid or a young adult?”.

    Your hobby doesn’t have to involve intense commitment. “Reading, gardening, dancing, listening to music, or simply spending time alone can be just as meaningful as running a marathon,” Snyder notes.

    Search online for local groups involved in the activity you want to pursue. Your local library may have resources to help you get started as well.

    When you’re ready to commit, set realistic goals. Start by focusing on your hobby consistently for just 10-15 minutes per day. Showing up is the main goal.

    It has been revealed that “Motherhood should expand a woman’s identity, not erase it,” Snyder advises. Which hobby will help expand yours?

    This ‘unhinged’ advice for toddler moms is actually pretty genius

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • They’re old enough to have opinions, verbal enough to pepper in words like “actually” and small enough to go fully boneless in the cereal aisle when overruled.
    • Recent findings suggest that A recent Threads post from @jayonathequeen asked parents for their best “unhinged advice” for raising toddlers, and the replies poured in.
    • Recent findings suggest that many of the suggestions are surprisingly hinged.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Toddlers are a wild ride. They’re old enough to have opinions, verbal enough to pepper in words like “actually” and small enough to go fully boneless in the cereal aisle when overruled. But with the right frame of mind and a little patience, we can outsmart them.

    Recent findings suggest that A recent Threads post from @jayonathequeen asked parents for their best “unhinged advice” for raising toddlers, and the replies poured in. Some came from toddler room teachers, longtime nannies and even doctors. Most came from moms who’ve logged countless hours negotiating with toddlers and consulting their pediatricians. We’ve all earned our stripes, and sometimes there’s nothing like raw mom-to-mom advice.

    Recent findings suggest that many of the suggestions are surprisingly hinged. And certainly no one’s judging.

    Recent findings suggest that anyone who has turned around in a parking lot to find an empty space where a small person used to be knows this particular brand of panic. The thread’s most-liked reply, with nearly 18,000 hearts, went straight at the escape artist problem, and the moms underneath it kept the ideas coming.

    Credit: @thriving_out_of_spite, @norcalcaro and @sksargeant via Threads.

    One mom’s solution doubled as entertainment.

    Credit: @champersstamers via Threads.

    (If you try this one, stick with a foil balloon, since popped latex is a choking hazard for little kids.).

    Toddler palates are a moving target. The food they inhaled one day is suddenly disgusting the next. A couple of moms found that a little creative branding goes a long way, at the table and beyond.

    Credit: @analee_inreallife via Threads.

    It has been revealed that brushing teeth, putting on shoes, surviving the checkout aisle. The daily stuff is where most battles originate, and, in turn, where moms get the most inventive. A common thread here is giving toddlers a sense of control while you cleverly steer the ship.

    Credit: @parentnest.digital via Threads.

    Credit: @suziespree via Threads.

    And sometimes the smartest move is picking your battles.

    Credit: @cryssinikki via Threads.

    When a meltdown hits, plenty of moms agreed the first move is regulating yourself. Toddlers take their emotional cues from us, so the calmer we stay, the faster they come back down.

    Credit: @sin_standard via Threads.

    From there, a little misdirection can work wonders.

    Credit: @thenerdyderma via Threads.

    Credit: @josephineadel via Threads.

    In a recent development, that sniff trick is a cousin of the viral “Jessica” trick, where a parent interrupts a meltdown by calmly calling for someone who isn’t there. Pediatrician Dr. Madison Szar told Motherly that “What’s that smell?” works just as well, since the surprise is what breaks the loop. Bonus points for the deep breaths.

    And for the moments when you’re the one about to lose it, one mom has a suggestion that sounds unhinged until you hear her out.

    Credit: @kaitlyn_e.a via Threads.

    It has been revealed that then there are the white lies. One bedtime fib stood out as particularly clever.

    Credit: @kellywills901 via Threads.

    In a recent development, having raised two kids, one in college and one in high school, I can attest that I lied to them. A lot. The car won’t start unless you’re buckled. It’s against the law to take your shoes off in the store. The toy store is closing, so we have to leave now. I promise you they are both 100% trustworthy, honest people.

    Sources indicate that when I was a fresh mom, just 21 and wildly out of my depth, I had a mentor with a toddler of her own. A yoga teacher who became a mom in her early 40s, she was a free spirit who didn’t mother through the lens of anyone else’s scrutiny. It was wild and refreshing.

    It has been revealed that she was willing to be inconvenienced so her son could explore and held firm when exploring teetered toward danger. She also leaned into the absurdity. At one point she’d somehow acquired a shopping cart, and when her son got grumpy, she’d load him in with a rug, some toys and their cat (I’m not kidding) and march around the neighborhood with the dog following behind.

    Toddlers are ridiculous, and we all know it. Sometimes you have to meet the moment with the same.

    Justice Department Unveils Results from Operation Not Forgotten 2026

    📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1367 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fbi

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Department of Justice and FBI unveiled today results of the personnel surge in support of Operation Not Forgotten 2026, which focuses on unresolved cases in Indian country with a priority on cases involving violence against women and children, including those who are missing or murdered.
    • In its fourth year, Operation Not Forgotten surged personnel and investigative resources across the country from April 1 through September 30, resulting in 118 arrests, 41 individuals charged federally, 25 child victims identified or located, and 72 weapons recovered.
    • It has been revealed that “The Department of Justice will always work to deliver justice for the victims of violent crime in Indian country,” stated Attorney General Todd Blanche.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Department of Justice and FBI unveiled today results of the personnel surge in support of Operation Not Forgotten 2026, which focuses on unresolved cases in Indian country with a priority on cases involving violence against women and children, including those who are missing or murdered.

    In its fourth year, Operation Not Forgotten surged personnel and investigative resources across the country from April 1 through September 30, resulting in 118 arrests, 41 individuals charged federally, 25 child victims identified or located, and 72 weapons recovered. FBI agents conducted 990 interviews and 232 search operations. Arrests increased by 123% and subjects charged by 52% over 2025.

    It has been revealed that “The Department of Justice will always work to deliver justice for the victims of violent crime in Indian country,” stated Attorney General Todd Blanche. “Thanks to the hard work of the FBI, our U.S. Attorneys, and other federal and tribal partners, Operation Not Forgotten and Operation Steadfast Promise are helping make communities safer and providing comfort for victims and families.”.

    Sources indicate that “This year’s Operation Not Forgotten continued this FBI’s largest commitment to Indian Country in the history of the Bureau,” remarked FBI Director Kash Patel. “The results were outstanding – from April 1 through September 30, this FBI worked more than 500 cases, a 59% increase from last year’s operation; 118 arrests, a 123% increase; and 41 subjects charged federally, a 52% increase. This is in addition to 25 child victims identified or located and 72 weapons recovered. These involved life-saving operations, with cases including child sexual abuse, physical assault and abuse, domestic violence, CSAM cases, and more.

    According to recent reports, “Operation Not Forgotten sends a loud and clear message that our long-forgotten partners in Indian Country are forgotten no more,” noted Director Patel. “When I assumed the position of FBI Director a year and a half ago, this FBI promised we would be there for our tribal partners. We have and will continue to be – through our 400 agents dedicated to Indian country, 30 Safe Trails Task Forces, and increased awareness with our Voices Not Forgotten program, where the FBI quadrupled the rewards to at least $25,000 for information associated with homicides, kidnappings and missing persons in Indian country. Thank you to our federal, state, and local partners who continue to work with us to ensure these unsolved crimes and cases receive the surge in resources they deserve.”.

    “Operation Not Forgotten demonstrates the Trump Administration’s commitment to protecting tribal communities, strengthening public safety, and ensuring that victims and their families have access to justice,” said Billy Kirkland, Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs, U.S. Department of the Interior. “Through close collaboration across the federal government and in partnership with tribal, state, and local law enforcement, we are bringing additional resources and investigative support to Indian Country to address violent crime, advance unresolved cases, and help families find answers. The Department of the Interior, through the Bureau of Indian Affairs, remains committed to working alongside our partners to deliver meaningful results and build safer communities for generations to come.".

    Examples of cases charged during this period include:.

    Sources indicate that in the District of Wyoming, the surge resulted in the federal indictment of 18 individuals for an array of violent crimes, and child abuse offenses on the Wind River Indian Reservation, including U.S. v. Jose Benito Ocon: This prosecution arises from an August 2025 incident near Riverton, where the defendant allegedly executed a male passenger with a gunshot to the head inside a moving vehicle before turning the firearm on two female witnesses. Leveraging the surge’s enhanced investigative assets, a grand jury returned an indictment charging the defendant with five felony counts, including first-degree murder, discharging a firearm during a crime of violence, and two distinct counts of assault with a dangerous weapon. He faces a mandatory sentence of life imprisonment if convicted. In U.S. v. Darlynn Sheree Seminole, federal prosecutors filed charges following a June 2026 domestic violence intervention by the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) Wind River Police Department, involving allegations of severe physical trauma inflicted on a 10-year-old.

    In the District of Nevada, in July a federal grand jury returned a superseding indictment charging Delshay Astor with the alleged murder of Anna Scott, a member of the Pyramid Lake Paiute Tribe, on the Reno-Sparks Indian Colony in February 2022, and also charged Joel Christy for assisting Astor to avoid apprehension.

    In the District of Minnesota, Operation Not Forgotten has resulted in four cases charged during the surge period with violent and sexual offenses in Indian Country, including sexual abuse of minors, domestic assault causing substantial bodily injury, assault by strangulation, and assault with intent to commit kidnapping. One recent case includes U.S. v. Courtney John Barrett Sr. indicted on September 22, 2026, on two counts of sexual abuse of a minor.

    It has been revealed that in the District of Montana, Michael Plentybuffalo was charged in the death of Shann Nomee, who went missing during an extreme cold snap in January 2024 and whose frozen body was found in a field north of Lodge Grass, Montana after a community led search and a tip to the Bureau of Indian Affairs that pointed to Plentybuffalo. His case is pending trial.

    Also in Montana, Lance Crookedarm was charged with the May 2026 violent assault and non-fatal strangulation of a female victim.

    In the District of Arizona, at least four cases were charged including two violent assaults, an arson, and the aggravated sexual abuse of a minor under 12, all of which occurred on the Navajo Nation, as well as an additional assault that was committed on the Fort Apache Indian Reservation.

    FBI’s Operation Steadfast Promise.

    It has been revealed that operation Steadfast Promise, first confirmed in 2026, is a continuing comprehensive surge of resources to address a wide range of violent criminal threats impacting Indian country. Operation Steadfast Promise builds on the successes of Operation Not Forgotten with the addition of multiple new initiatives to improve public safety in Tribal communities. The FBI, in coordination with U.S. Attorneys’ Offices, the Bureau of Indian Affairs Missing and Murdered Unit, Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and Tribal and other federal law enforcement partners, is working across multiple territories to bring investigative aid to cases and resolution for victims and their families. Since Operation Steadfast Promise began in April, the FBI opened over 1,200 new investigations in Indian country, obtained criminal charges on 678 subjects, made over 700 arrests, recovered 2,260 weapons, and made 140 drug seizures.

    This year, Operation Not Forgotten continued to address the over 4,000 open investigations in Indian country including death investigations, child abuse cases, domestic violence, and adult sexual abuse investigations, underscoring the persistent and urgent need for sustained resource investment in these communities.

    During Operation Not Forgotten, the FBI surged personnel, including investigative, intelligence, and other support personnel, on rotating temporary duty assignments across Indian country in twelve FBI field offices, in Albuquerque, Billings, Detroit, Denver, Jackson, Las Vegas, Minneapolis, Oklahoma City, Omaha, Portland, Phoenix and Salt Lake City. Working in close coordination with Tribal law enforcement agencies, the BIA Missing and Murdered Unit, and U.S. Attorneys' Offices, together law enforcement worked to advance open investigations and pursue accountability for victims and their families.

    Additionally, the FBI has brought focus to a newly introduced FBI’s Voices Not Forgotten webpage that includes a searchable and interactive map that brings attention to FBI investigations in Indian country where the FBI, in coordination with state, local and Tribal law enforcement are seeking the public’s assistance. In August 2026, the FBI announced the establishment of a new protocol which created a minimum reward of up to $25,000 for all publicly advertised cases involving homicides, kidnappings and missing persons in Indian country where the FBI has assumed jurisdiction.

    According to recent reports, the FBI remains committed to standing alongside Tribal communities, federal partners, and local law enforcement to address the violent crime threats that continue to impact Indian country. To learn more, visit www.fbi.gov/investigate/violent-crime/indian-country-crime.

    The FBI encourages anyone with information related to unresolved violent crimes in Indian country to contact their local FBI field office or submit a tip at https://tips.fbi.gov.

    #8985. Tech Report: The Silent Health Problem Vets Say Most Cat Owners Never See Coming

    📅 14 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1325 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Catster ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: The Silent Health Problem Vets Say Most Cat Owners Never See Coming

    📅 14 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1325 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Catster

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that catster is reader-supported.
    • It has been revealed that dental disease is one of the most common health problems seen by vets, yet it's also one of the easiest to overlook.
    • By the time obvious signs appear, the problem may already have been developing for months or even longer, and suddenly a minor issue is a major disaster.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that catster is reader-supported. When you buy via links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission at no cost to you. Learn more.

    It has been revealed that dental disease is one of the most common health problems seen by vets, yet it's also one of the easiest to overlook. Cats are particularly good at hiding discomfort, so a cat with painful teeth or inflamed gums may carry on behaving normally for a surprisingly long time.

    By the time obvious signs appear, the problem may already have been developing for months or even longer, and suddenly a minor issue is a major disaster. The good news is that dental disease is largely preventable, and keeping a cat's teeth healthy doesn't necessarily mean relying on a toothbrush alone.

    Plaque is where the problem begins. It forms when bacteria mix with saliva and food particles on the surface of the teeth. If plaque isn't removed, it can harden into tartar â aka calculus â within days.

    Tartar leads to inflammation of the gums, a condition known as gingivitis. This can progress to periodontitis, an infection involving the tooth root, weakening the attachment between the gum and the tooth, and eroding enamel. Eventually, the tooth starts breaking down from the inside.

    In a recent development, these conditions can all be painful. A cat with advanced dental disease may drool, paw at its mouth, drop food while eating, or stop eating altogether. Bad breath, bloody saliva, teeth chattering, and even sneezing can also be warning signs.

    Unfortunately, cats don't always make their discomfort obvious, which is why prevention is so important.

    According to recent reports, regular toothbrushing remains the most effective way to prevent dental disease in cats. Daily brushing removes plaque before it has the chance to harden into tartar and tackles one of the main causes of dental problems.

    Industry observers note that A toothbrush or finger brush designed for cats should be used with toothpaste specifically formulated for felines. Human toothpaste contains ingredients that can be harmful if swallowed.

    Recent findings suggest that it's much easier to establish the habit when a cat is young, making it an enjoyable, even fun part of their routine. Older cats can learn too, although a slow approach with plenty of positive reinforcement gives the best chance of success.

    Even brushing every few days is better than not brushing at all, although daily brushing provides the greatest benefit.

    For cats that arenât tolerating a brush, dental wipes can be a good option.

    It has been revealed that for cats that won't tolerate brushing, dental diets and treats can provide another option. Dental dry foods contain ingredients and have a texture that are designed to help reduce plaque formation. The limitation is that not every cat actually chews its food. Some cats swallow their food with very little chewing, which reduces the potential benefit.

    When choosing dental products, the Veterinary Oral Health Council seal is a useful indicator of effectiveness. Products carrying the VOHC seal have been independently tested and shown to reduce plaque or tartar.

    According to recent reports, prescription dental diets are also available through veterinarians. They typically use oversized kibble designed to encourage more contact with the teeth during chewing and may be worth considering for cats with a history of dental problems.

    It has been revealed that dental treats and chews have a similar action to dental diets, but are often made from more palatable ingredients to encourage cats to chew them. As a result, they can be quite high in calories, so make sure you include them in your catâs daily allowance.

    More recently, powders containing brown algae or seaweed have been showing promising results in the fight against tartar formation, but some cats arenât keen on the taste.

    Sources indicate that oral rinses offer another preventative option for cats that resist brushing and aren't suitable for dietary changes. They can be applied using gauze or a soft cloth and work by chemically reducing plaque and tartar before they build up.

    Recent findings suggest that the VOHC seal can again help when choosing between products. A veterinarian can also recommend an appropriate rinse for an individual cat.

    Water additives are one of the easiest dental care options because they are simply added to a cat's drinking water. They work by helping inhibit plaque formation.

    There are some key limitations, however. A cat that doesn't drink enough water may not receive much benefit, while some additives can change the smell or taste of the water enough that a cat avoids drinking it.

    A VOHC-approved water additive can be a useful addition to a broader dental care routine, but it is unlikely to be enough on its own.

    It has been revealed that plaque prevention gels are often used after a professional dental cleaning. They can help protect newly cleaned teeth and extend the time before another cleaning is needed.

    Veterinarians commonly recommend these gels as a follow-up to professional dental treatment rather than as a standalone daily solution. Any instructions about feeding and drinking after application should be followed carefully.

    According to recent reports, even cats receiving regular dental care at home may eventually need a professional cleaning. This is performed under general anesthesia, allowing the veterinarian to clean below the gum line, examine each tooth closely, take dental X-rays when necessary, and identify teeth that need to be removed.

    The need for anesthesia can understandably concern some owners, but untreated dental disease can lead to chronic pain, infection, and systemic illness.

    In a recent development, senior cats and cats with a history of dental problems may also need their teeth assessed more frequently than during a standard annual examination. Finding problems early generally means treatment can be simpler and less invasive.

    According to recent reports, there has been a rise in the number of businesses offering dentals without anesthesia, at a price much lower than a dental procedure with your vet. While the idea of a cheaper dental cleaning without the worry of your cat going under anesthetic is appealing, the most significant periodontal disease happens below the gumline. Cats in particular are susceptible to a painful condition known as feline oral resorptive lesions (FORLs), in which the tooth slowly dissolves. FORLs can develop in completely clean teeth. They often form in the roots and need to be diagnosed using dental x-ray.

    A catâs teeth may look clean after an anesthetic-free dental, but there could be painful problems going on beneath the surface.

    It has been revealed that dental disease isn't inevitable, but preventing it requires more than waiting for obvious symptoms to appear. Cats can hide dental pain remarkably well, meaning a seemingly healthy mouth may already have problems developing beneath the surface.

    Regular brushing is the most effective option, but dental diets, treats, rinses, water additives, and professional cleaning can all play a role. The right combination will depend on the individual cat and how well they tolerate each approach.

    Keeping on top of dental care can help prevent painful problems from becoming something a cat has to quietly live with for years.

    How to thank school support staff this American Education Week (Hint: It’s not a mug)

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (592 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mother

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, my son’s favorite person in elementary school was the nurse.
    • That nurse lovingly cared for kids who needed far more support than my son did.
    • People like her have a name in education circles.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, my son’s favorite person in elementary school was the nurse. She was warm and welcoming, always quick with a comforting hug. More importantly, she had the best Band-Aids in the building, and she wasn’t stingy about giving them out. A scraped knee got one. So did a paper cut, and even some invisible injuries, too. She knew when a kid headed to see her, it wasn’t necessarily about needing that Band-Aid.

    That nurse lovingly cared for kids who needed far more support than my son did. There were kids who came to her office with a belly ache that wasn’t a stomach bug, but because they hadn’t had breakfast, and possibly dinner either. There were kids who could barely stay awake in class because they’d spent the night in a car instead of a bed. She met those kids with the same warmth she gave my Band-Aid collector, and I’m certain she kept a stash of snacks in her desk for those visits in particular.

    People like her have a name in education circles. They’re education support professionals, or ESPs, and they include school nurses, cafeteria workers, bus drivers, security staff, paraeducators, technical personnel, custodians, skilled trade workers, and front office staff. Ask kids about their favorite grown-up at school, and there’s a decent chance the answer is one of them.

    The people our kids adore are often the people schools pay the least. Nearly 32% of full-time ESPs earn less than $25,000 a year, according to the National Education Association, and on average, they’re paid below a living wage in all 50 states.

    That’s not a livable wage in most areas. “Our wages are so low, we are forced to have two or three jobs,” paraeducator Yahaira Rodriguez told NEA Today. The nurse who stays late with a hungry kid may be heading to a second job after school, eating dinner in the car on the way. That’s a long day for someone whose job is to take care of everyone else’s kids. It also makes it hard to stay in the job. Before the 2024–25 school year, 69% of public schools reported trouble filling at least one non-teaching position, according to the National Center for Education Statistics. That means the kids who rely on them the most are the ones who lose out when they leave or the positions can’t be filled.

    Recent findings suggest that the NEA ESP Bill of Rights lays out what these professionals need to stay in the jobs our kids depend on. Developed by ESPs themselves, it asks for pay that covers the bills without a second job, health care they can afford and a workplace ‘free of violence, including physical, verbal, and emotional abuse.’ It’s a practical document about what it takes to keep these jobs filled. The full list includes:.

    Since the movement began, 18 states have debuted ESP Bill of Rights campaigns, according to NEA.

    Sources indicate that american Education Week runs November 16 to 20, 2026, and this year NEA is using it to honor education support staff. Here are a few ways to show up for the people who show up for our kids:.

    Recent findings suggest that our kids won’t remember most of what happened at school, but they’ll remember who was kind to them there. For a lot of them, that’s a nurse, a cafeteria staff or a bus driver doing the job on less than a living wage. Sign the ESP Bill of Rights pledge and help them stay.

    #8979. E-bike safety for kids: What pediatric ER doctors want parents to know before gifting one

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1075 w)
